anti_overlap: Do not evaluate Bp/rng crate-separation, numeric port fidelity, phase-order bugs, or the cycle/week time-unit mismatch — those are fd-simcore-fixedpoint-determinism's exclusive focus; only touch ordering/numerics here insofar as they reveal a vocabulary leak (e.g. a raven-tuned constant hardcoded outside vocab/).

Do not run the CUJ-to-work-item traceability sweep (recruitment-after-death, interest formula, closed-decision coverage) as a standalone completeness audit — that is fd-cuj-traceability-completeness's focus; only raise a CUJ point here when it's specifically evidence of a vocabulary-agnosticism gap (e.g. the interest mechanic being raven-specific despite living in the 'agnostic' engine).

Do not assess whether the raven vocabulary's OWN mechanics (breakdown thresholds, scar-pull magnitude) are correctly ported from the TS source — that's a fidelity concern for the other lens; this lens only cares whether those mechanics are properly walled off from the engine core.
decision_lens: Treat every struct/enum/function signature in cast.rs, needs.rs, sim.rs as a claim of the form 'this generalizes over any vocabulary' and actively try to construct the vocabulary that breaks it — not just the WI-8 test's own convenient throwaway rat vocabulary, but the actually-planned future ones (octopus - radically different body/need topology; rats - colony/pack dynamics) named in the ruling this plan cites. A proof that only exercises a vocabulary shaped like a slightly-renamed raven is not a proof.
focus: Game-systems design review of whether animal-sim's public API and WI-8's proof genuinely demonstrate vocabulary-agnosticism, or whether raven-specific assumptions (the DF-lineage vise, boldness/scar coupling, single-need-polarity, dispatch-verb shape) are structurally baked into the 'agnostic' engine layer.
name: fd-gamedesign-vocab-agnosticism
persona: Apply the perspective of a systems designer/engineer who has built and later had to generalize a game engine's core loop for a second, materially different content pack — someone who has been burned by a first 'plugin API' that looked generic but actually encoded the first game's assumptions (a single scalar difficulty knob, an implicit two-need model, an event vocabulary shaped by one game's UI) and had to do a painful breaking rewrite when the second consumer arrived.
review_areas: WI-8's chosen second vocabulary (a '2-need rat' with different drain rates and scar kinds) — does varying only drain-rate scalars and scar-kind strings actually stress the parts of the API that are raven-shaped, or does it dodge the hard axes (Needs is a hardcoded 4-field struct {food,water,health,interest} in WI-3 — can a vocabulary with a DIFFERENT need count/shape, e.g. octopus's likely different sensory/need axes, or a colony-level need like rats' pack cohesion, be expressed at all without editing needs.rs, or does 'vocabulary-agnostic' silently mean 'agnostic within raven's exact 4-need topology'?

AnimalState::Foraging is the ONLY non-idle/non-dead state in cast.rs (WI-5) — does this foreclose a vocabulary whose core verb isn't 'forage a ground' (e.g. an octopus vocabulary built around hiding/camouflage, or a rat vocabulary built around burrowing/colony logistics) without an engine-level edit, meaning the 'agnostic' state machine is actually a raven-forage state machine with a generic-sounding name?

TraitSet as 'a generic bag the vocabulary fills' (WI-5) — is this actually unconstrained, or does effective_boldness's signature (reads traits+scars -> a single Bp) hardcode the assumption that every vocabulary's disposition collapses to ONE scalar boldness axis, which is a raven/DF-vise-specific idea (bold vs timid) that a colony-based rat vocabulary or a multi-axis octopus vocabulary might not share?

Scar { kind: String, from: String } as the 'vocabulary-agnostic' scar shape — does the engine's breakdown/death logic (WI-7 step 4/5) ever pattern-match on a raven-specific scar kind STRING (e.g. "gaunt") inside sim.rs/needs.rs rather than only through the vocabulary's effective_boldness function, which would mean the engine is not actually blind to raven's vocabulary despite the stringly-typed appearance of genericity?

The grief-scar mechanic (WI-7 step 5: 'a death grieves the whole flock' as a v1 provisional) — is 'grieving the whole flock' itself a raven-specific (murder/flock) social assumption wired into the AGNOSTIC engine's death-handling code, rather than being vocabulary-supplied? If sim.rs's death-check hardcodes 'every survivor gains a grieving scar,' a colony vocabulary (rats) or a solitary-vocabulary (octopus, non-social) would have this behavior forced on it regardless of whether it fits.

The dispatch/forage-only verb surface: is 'Dispatch { animal, ground }' (WI-7) the whole verb vocabulary the agnostic engine supports, and if so, does that quietly assume every future vocabulary's core interaction is spatial-forage-dispatch — worth checking against what is actually knowable about octopus/rat vocabularies from the plan's own citations (R12, ruling) versus what's asserted with no support.
severity_examples: P0 (block-execution): if Needs is a fixed 4-field struct and there is no described mechanism (generic parameter, trait, variable-length map) for a second vocabulary to declare a DIFFERENT need topology, then WI-8's acceptance criterion ('touches only vocab/, no engine-internal edits') is unfalsifiable by construction — any vocabulary the test author picks will trivially satisfy it because the test author is free to only ever pick vocabularies that fit raven's 4-need shape. This makes the R12 proof structurally circular and should be called out as blocking before the crate is built with Needs hardcoded this way.

P1 (must fix before implementing): AnimalState::Foraging as the only working verb bakes 'forage a ground' into the engine layer; if octopus or rats need a structurally different core verb, cast.rs/sim.rs will need an engine-level edit when that day comes, contradicting the plan's own claim that vocab/ additions never touch cast.rs/sim.rs — this is an assertion the plan makes about the future that its own WI-5 design already falsifies.

P2 (degrades quality): 'a death grieves the whole flock' as an engine-level default (not vocabulary-supplied) will need to be ripped out or special-cased the moment a non-social vocabulary (octopus) is added, since a solitary animal has no flock to grieve — flag as a vocabulary leak now while it's cheap to make the grief-scar behavior vocabulary-supplied instead of engine-hardcoded.
success_hints: Names a specific, concrete vocabulary shape (not just 'octopus' as a label) that the stated API (Needs struct, AnimalState enum, TraitSet, Scar) cannot express without an engine edit, and shows exactly which struct/enum field forces the edit.
Distinguishes 'this is agnostic in letter (generic type names) but not in spirit (only one shape fits)' from genuine structural agnosticism, citing the specific WI section.

Proposes the minimal API change (e.g. Needs as a generic map/vec instead of a fixed struct, or a vocabulary-supplied death-consequence hook instead of hardcoded grief) that would make WI-8's proof non-circular, rather than only diagnosing the gap.
Explicitly checks whether the WI-8 test's chosen throwaway vocabulary was picked BECAUSE it happens to fit the existing shape, and calls that out as evidence the test is a fig leaf if so.
task_context: Adversarially review this execution-grade build plan for RaveNous's survival floor BEFORE a coding agent executes it. The plan creates a new deterministic Rust crate 'animal-sim' as a vocabulary-agnostic substrate (needs/foraging/scars/permadeath; raven is the first vocabulary, octopus/rats are future vocabularies). It ports a proven-but-retired TypeScript survival loop (lib/cycle.ts, lib/flock.ts, lib/fields/food.ts) into fixed-point Rust. Focus the lenses on: (1) is the animal-sim/city-sim separation correct — no dependency + duplicated Bp fixed-point, or a drift trap? (2) is determinism airtight given the ruling that a save = deterministic replay, when two engines with independent seed streams must later be composed? (3) is porting truncating-integer basis points (float 0.28 -> Bp 2800) behavior-preserving vs the TS floats? (4) is the WI-8 vocabulary-agnosticism test a real proof or a fig leaf — what raven assumption leaks into the 'agnostic' engine? (5) is step_cycle's phase order (dispatch->return->drain->breakdown->death) free of ordering bugs? (6) is the 'cycle' vs city-sim 'week' time-unit mismatch a landmine deferred too casually? (7) what do the ratified CUJs (docs/cujs/ravenous-00*, ravenous-04) demand that the plan is missing — recruitment-after-death has no work item, the interest mechanic is a formula-less provisional. Rank findings by severity and flag block-execution vs follow-up. The ratified CUJs and the city-sim engine (../infinite-fun-space-app/crates/city-sim/src/) are the ground truth.
